name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Run a **7-day rolling A/B test on 150k clips**, swapping 30% weekly between two creative agent pipelines. This balances speed and statistical power: shorter than 14 days but longer than 10, with higher swap rate to catch trends faster. Trade-off: risk of false positives from smaller sample windows, but we mitigate with strict p-value thresholds and manual review for outliers. **Creative Ops Lead owns the test design and artifact (dashboard + report).**

name: Scriv
text: The 7-day rolling A/B test cuts cycle time but amplifies false positives—smaller windows inflate noise, especially for late-cycle spikes. Better: run a **10-day fixed test with 20% weekly swaps**, locking the window to stabilize signals while still catching trends. Settle it with a side-by-side pilot on 100k clips; the one with lower false-positive rate wins.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a **10-day fixed A/B test on 150k clips**, swapping 20% weekly. This locks the window to stabilize signals, cutting false positives from Reel’s 7-day rolling test while still catching trends faster than Scriv’s fixed 10-day with 30% swaps. Trade-off: slower cycle time than Reel’s approach, but the cleaner data outweighs the delay.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s 10-day fixed test on 150k clips still risks overfitting to short-term noise—rolling swaps spread risk better than fixed windows. Run a **14-day fixed test with 15% weekly swaps** instead: longer windows stabilize signals, lower swap rate reduces false positives, and the trade-off is only 4 extra days. Settle it by comparing false-positive rates in side-by-side pilot runs.

name: Scope
text: Run a **14-day fixed A/B test on 100k clips**, swapping 15% weekly between pipelines. This locks the window to stabilize signals, cutting false positives from shorter tests while still catching trends faster than fixed 10-day tests. Trade-off: slower cycle time than rolling tests, but the trade-off is worth it for cleaner data. Chisel owns execution.

name: Scriv
text: Scope’s 14-day fixed test on 100k clips cuts false positives but risks missing late-cycle spikes—errors that spike in the final 24 hours still blow up after day 10. Run a **10-day fixed test with 20% weekly swaps on 150k clips**, locked to stabilize signals, and settle it with a side-by-side pilot against the 14-day plan.
